[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural image.
Keep the reference plate's exact composition: every edge, horizon line, and object position stays where it is.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   Parkland garden enclosure comprising dormant perennial turf (*Lolium perenne*, *Festuca rubra*). Urban canopy: Mature *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane) and *Tilia cordata* (small-leaved lime). Phenological state for late December: Complete winter defoliation, exposed branching networks, dormant terminal buds, zero foliage.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
LIGHTING: 2200K Blue Hour Civil Twilight. Sun elevation -0.4°. Zero direct sunlight. Extinguish daytime cast shadows. Diffuse indigo ambient skylight with soft contact occlusion.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
A static architectural survey of Charlotte Square, Edinburgh. In the center stands West Register House, an 1814 Neo-Classical church facade constructed of fine-grained Craigleith pale buff sandstone ashlar, featuring a colossal tetrastyle portico with unfluted columns, rusticated podium, dentilled pediment, and a monumental ribbed copper dome patinated to rich verdigris green, capped with an octagonal stone cupola and gilded cross. Flanking the central edifice are symmetrical Robert Adam Georgian terraces: 3-storey ashlar facades with rusticated basements, precise string courses, 12-over-12 and 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case windows, balustraded roof parapets, and pitched Ballachulish slate mansards punctuated by ashlar chimney stacks. In the garden foreground stands the Prince Albert Memorial: an equestrian bronze statue with deep brown-green oxidation set upon an architectural stepped pedestal of polished pink granite and tooled sandstone. The foreground consists of a broad expanse of manicured winter lawn bounded by gravel perimeter pathways. Scattered across the garden are mature *Platanus × acerifolia* and *Tilia cordata* trees in full December dormancy, exhibiting bare, intricate branch silhouettes completely devoid of foliage. Crisp vertical masonry alignments, planar ashlar joints, fine tooling marks, cast-iron spearhead railings, and authentic carbonaceous stone weathering across architectural moldings.
